$comment: Mission 1.65. The verdict, the two envelope states, and the handoff.
mission: 1.65 — Dual Enquiry Dispatch Envelope Preparation V1
primary_outcome_statement: The ONYPHE enquiry is drafted, frozen and hashed, its recipient is established from two first-party pages that print it as a live link, and its dispatch envelope is complete and awaiting one operator approval. The Netlas enquiry is unchanged and still hash-verified, and its envelope stays a template because the one field it needs is an address only a person reading the provider's page can supply. Nothing was sent.

why_this_outcome_and_not_another.why_not_A: Outcome A needs both recipients established and both envelopes complete. The Netlas recipient is not supplied.
why_this_outcome_and_not_another.why_not_C: Outcome C is the inverse of what happened: it describes Netlas complete and ONYPHE's channel unfindable. The ONYPHE channel was found and the Netlas one was not.
why_this_outcome_and_not_another.why_not_D: Outcome D needs neither recipient established. One is.
why_this_outcome_and_not_another.why_not_E: Outcome E is for recipients known with no permitted channel bindable. A channel is bound for the one recipient that is known: the operator sending it manually.
why_this_outcome_and_not_another.why_not_F: The Netlas body still hashes to the approved value.
why_this_outcome_and_not_another.why_not_G: All three ONYPHE questions were expressible without changing the frozen construct and without asking for data. The construct is not mentioned in the enquiry at all.

envelopes.note: The sender is a permitted placeholder for manual send, so the hash binds three of four fields. Its cost is stated in the envelope.

the_asymmetry_and_why_it_is_not_a_prefer.$comment: One apparatus is dispatch-ready and the other is not, and that is a fact about two publishers' contact pages.
the_asymmetry_and_why_it_is_not_a_prefer.observation: One provider prints its contact address as a live link on two pages. The other serves its address through an anti-scraping mechanism. Nothing about either fact bears on whether the apparatus is a good measurement instrument.
the_asymmetry_and_why_it_is_not_a_prefer.not_a_ranking: Both apparatuses remain INDIVIDUALLY_UNRESOLVED or worse, and no pair gate was evaluated. That one enquiry can move first is an accident of publishing practice.
the_asymmetry_and_why_it_is_not_a_prefer.the_temptation_declined: It would be easy to read dispatch readiness as progress on the apparatus. It is progress on the ASKING, and the gates are exactly where Mission 1.64 left them.

apparatus_states_unchanged.$comment: Part G. Recorded as a table so a reader can see that nothing moved.
apparatus_states_unchanged.rule: Question drafted is not answered, question approved is not answered, question sent is not answered.

one_approval_is_available_now.approval_string_form: APPROVE MISSION 1.65 DISPATCH <sha256 of the envelope>
one_approval_is_available_now.what_it_authorises: sending the frozen ONYPHE text once, to the established recipient, by the operator manually

one_input_is_still_missing.how_the_operator_supplies_it: open https://netlas.io/legal/ in a browser, where the address renders, and give the exact displayed string
one_input_is_still_missing.then: the envelope completes, is hashed, and gets its own approval string

next_mission_recommendation.name: Mission 1.66 — Approved Dispatch Execution V1
it_should: send exactly the envelopes whose hashes the operator approved, once each
record delivery provenance: channel, sender, recipient, time, and a message identifier where one exists
stop after sending, because reviewing a reply is a separate step that belongs after receipt
it_must_not: send an envelope whose hash was not approved
infer authorisation from content approval, a connected account or an instruction to continue
treat a dispatch as an answer or an answer as a PASS before review
request data, access, a trial or pricing in any accompanying message

stop_condition.awaiting: one dispatch approval, and one address
